props.heading: Software Monetization Readiness Assessment
props.description: Evaluate your organization's software monetization maturity and benchmark against industry peers and get actionable recommendations to maximize revenue.
props.startNote: Join hundreds of growth leaders who have benchmarked their monetization maturity.
props.categoriesHeading: Your Category Scores vs. Industry Benchmarks
props.gateText: Get a professional PDF with detailed recommendations, industry benchmarks, and a personalised action plan.
props.ctaHeading: Ready to Transform Your Software Monetization?
props.ctaText: Thales Software Monetization solutions help you protect, package, and monetize your software with industry-leading licensing and entitlement management.

props.label: One Product
props.description: We sell a single software product or solution

props.label: A Few Related Products
props.description: We sell several products that are part of one product family

props.label: Multiple Product Lines
props.description: We sell different product lines managed by one team or division

props.label: Many Products Across Teams
props.description: We sell many product lines managed by different teams or divisions

props.question: How many software products does your organization sell?
props.description: This helps us understand the complexity of your software business. Think about all the distinct software products or solutions your company offers to customers.

props.label: One Way Only
props.description: Customers use our software in only one way — either installed locally or accessed online (cloud/SaaS)

props.label: Two Options
props.description: Customers can choose between two options, such as cloud/SaaS and installed on their own servers

props.label: Three Options
props.description: We support cloud/SaaS, on-site installation, and hosting in the customer's own private cloud

props.label: All Options Available
props.description: We support cloud, on-site, private cloud, and software built into physical devices or equipment

props.question: How do your customers access and run your software?
props.description: Software can be delivered in different ways. Select the option that best describes how your customers use your products today.

props.label: 1–2 Ways
props.description: For example, only a one-time purchase, or only a subscription

props.label: 3–4 Ways
props.description: A mix, like subscriptions plus per-user pricing plus one-time purchase

props.label: 5–6 Ways
props.description: A broader mix that may include pay-per-use or token/credit-based access

props.label: 7 or More Ways
props.description: A comprehensive offering including pay-for-results, consumption billing, and more

props.question: How many different ways can customers buy or pay for your software?
props.description: Pricing models include things like one-time purchases, subscriptions, per-user fees, or pay-per-use. The more options you offer, the more flexibility customers have.

props.label: Not Working Well
props.description: We lose deals or get frequent complaints about our pricing and licensing

props.label: Needs Improvement
props.description: We know there are problems, but we're getting by

props.label: It's Okay
props.description: No major issues, but we're not fully confident it's optimal

props.label: Working Well
props.description: Our approach meets most needs with only minor improvements needed

props.question: How well is your current pricing and licensing approach working for your business?
props.description: Think about whether your pricing keeps up with how customers want to buy, whether it's easy to manage internally, and whether it supports your revenue goals.

props.label: Very Limited
props.description: Customers must accept fixed terms — no choice in pricing model or plan changes

props.label: Some Choice
props.description: Customers can pick from a few options when ordering, but can't change later

props.label: Good Flexibility
props.description: Customers can choose and adjust their plan or model, with some self-service options

props.label: Full Flexibility
props.description: Customers can switch plans, scale up or down, and manage everything through self-service

props.question: How much choice and flexibility do your customers have in how they purchase and use your software?
props.description: Customers increasingly expect to choose their pricing model, switch between plans, and manage licenses on their own. How well do you support this?

props.label: No Plan Yet
props.description: Each product is priced and sold independently with no coordinated strategy

props.label: Starting to Think About It
props.description: We're exploring the idea but haven't started implementing anything

props.label: Plan in Progress
props.description: We've defined a strategy and are beginning to put it into practice

props.label: Fully in Place
props.description: We have a comprehensive strategy that's actively driving revenue growth

props.question: Does your organization have a plan for how to package and price products together across your portfolio?
props.description: A portfolio monetization strategy is a coordinated plan for pricing, bundling, and selling your products together to grow revenue — rather than treating each product in isolation.

props.label: No — Separate Purchases Only
props.description: Each product must be purchased and licensed independently

props.label: For Some Products
props.description: A few products can be bundled or purchased together

props.label: For Most Products
props.description: Most of our products can be bundled or sold under shared agreements

props.label: Fully Unified
props.description: Customers can access our entire portfolio through unified licensing and bundles

props.question: Can your customers buy access to multiple products under a single license or agreement?
props.description: Instead of requiring separate purchases for each product, some vendors offer bundles, enterprise agreements, or shared credits that span multiple products.

props.label: Mostly Manual
props.description: We rely on spreadsheets, emails, or manual steps for most licensing tasks

props.label: Partially Automated
props.description: Some tasks are automated, but about half still require manual work

props.label: Mostly Automated
props.description: Most tasks are automated, with only a few manual steps remaining

props.label: Fully Automated
props.description: Everything from provisioning to renewals is automated end-to-end

props.question: How much of your license management is handled automatically vs. manually?
props.description: This covers tasks like issuing license keys, tracking who's using what, handling renewals, and managing upgrades. Manual processes slow things down and introduce errors.

props.label: No — Data Is Scattered
props.description: Information is spread across disconnected systems and teams with no unified view

props.label: Partial View
props.description: We can see some data in one place, but major gaps and disconnected systems remain

props.label: Mostly Complete View
props.description: We have a central platform for most data, with a few remaining gaps

props.label: Full Visibility
props.description: We have a single system that shows all licensing, usage, and purchase data in one place

props.question: Can you easily see a complete picture of who is using your software, how much, and what they've purchased?
props.description: Many companies have licensing data spread across different tools and teams, making it hard to track usage, identify upsell opportunities, or prevent churn.

props.label: No AI Features Yet
props.description: We haven't added AI capabilities to our products

props.label: Still Figuring It Out
props.description: We have or plan to have AI features, but haven't decided how to charge for them

props.label: Basic Approach
props.description: AI features are included in premium tiers, or sold as a paid add-on

props.label: Advanced Approach
props.description: We charge for AI based on actual usage, outcomes delivered, or through tiered consumption models

props.question: If your software includes AI-powered features, how are you charging for them?
props.description: As AI capabilities are added to software products, vendors need to decide how to price these features — whether to include them for free, charge extra, or create entirely new pricing models.

props.insight: Your limited product range restricts cross-sell opportunities. Consider expanding deployment options.
props.whatItMeans: {company}'s limited product portfolio or single delivery model restricts your ability to serve diverse customer needs. With 80% of vendors now offering SaaS, customers expect choice in how they deploy and consume software. Expanding your portfolio structure opens new market segments and customer conversations.
props.recommendations:
• Survey your top 20 customers to understand unmet deployment needs — 80% of vendors now offer SaaS, and customers who can't access your software their preferred way often choose a competitor instead
  • Map out which customer segments need cloud, on-premises, or hybrid access and create a 6-month roadmap to address the biggest gap first
  • Evaluate whether adjacent products or add-ons could expand your offering — even a simple complementary tool can increase average deal size by 15–25%

props.insight: Solid foundation — standardize delivery across product lines for a more consistent customer experience.
props.whatItMeans: {company} has a reasonable portfolio foundation, but there's room to broaden your deployment options or product mix. Customers increasingly want to choose between cloud, on-premises, and hybrid deployment at the time of use — not just at purchase time.
props.recommendations:
• Standardize how you deliver software across product lines so customers get a consistent experience — inconsistency creates support costs and slows deals
  • Investigate a unified entitlement platform that manages all products in one place, reducing the operational overhead of maintaining separate systems per product

props.insight: Strong portfolio breadth. Leverage it for enterprise bundles and portfolio-wide licensing agreements.
props.whatItMeans: {company}'s diverse portfolio and deployment options position you well. Your broad offering creates opportunities for cross-selling, bundling, and enterprise agreements that smaller portfolios can't support.
props.recommendations:
• Use your broad portfolio as a competitive weapon — create tiered enterprise bundles that lock in larger, longer-term commitments from your biggest customers
  • Develop portfolio-wide licensing agreements that let customers access any product under a single contract, simplifying procurement and driving expansion

props.action: Audit your deployment options and customer demand
props.detail: Survey your top 20 customers on unmet deployment needs. 80% of vendors now offer SaaS — if you don't, you're likely losing deals to competitors who do.

props.action: Leverage portfolio breadth for enterprise bundling
props.detail: Your portfolio structure is strong. Create tiered enterprise bundles that lock in larger, longer-term commitments and use your breadth as a competitive differentiator.

props.insight: Limited pricing options may be costing you deals. Adding subscription or usage-based models can reduce churn.
props.whatItMeans: {company}'s limited pricing options are likely costing you deals. 49% of vendors are dissatisfied with their licensing approach — if your pricing feels rigid or outdated compared to competitors, customers will notice.
props.recommendations:
• Add at least one subscription or term-based pricing option within the next 90 days — 73% of leading vendors already offer this, and it reduces customer risk, which accelerates deals
  • Introduce a usage-based or pay-as-you-go model for at least one product — this gives price-sensitive customers a low-risk entry point and creates natural expansion revenue
  • Audit your current pricing against your top 3 competitors — if customers can get more flexible terms elsewhere, you're losing deals you may not even know about

props.insight: Good model diversity. Pilot token-based or consumption pricing to differentiate from competitors.
props.whatItMeans: {company} offers a reasonable range of pricing models but isn't yet matching the variety offered by leading vendors. 73% of top-performing vendors offer subscription/term licensing.
props.recommendations:
• Pilot a token or credit-based model that lets customers consume services flexibly across products — this differentiates you and creates a built-in upsell mechanism
  • Automate license provisioning so new customers are activated in minutes instead of days — every delay between purchase and first use risks buyer's remorse

props.insight: Advanced pricing portfolio. Explore outcome-based pricing to command premium positioning.
props.whatItMeans: {company}'s diverse licensing portfolio is a significant competitive advantage. You can meet customers where they are — whether they prefer perpetual, subscription, usage-based, or hybrid models.
props.recommendations:
• Run a pricing optimization analysis on your top revenue products — even a 3–5% price increase backed by value metrics can significantly boost margins without affecting volume
  • Pilot outcome-based pricing for your highest-value offering — charging based on results delivered (not features used) commands premium pricing and deepens customer commitment

props.detail: 73% of leading vendors offer subscription licensing. Adding even one flexible model can reduce churn and increase deal velocity by giving customers a lower-risk entry point.
Your licensing maturity is solid. Differentiate further by piloting outcome-based pricing for high-value customers — charging based on results delivered commands premium positioning.

props.insight: Customers likely face friction buying and managing your software. Self-service portals reduce churn risk.
props.whatItMeans: {company}'s customers are likely experiencing friction when buying and managing your software. 69% of customers want more flexible license models, and 61% want better visibility into what they've purchased vs. what they're using.
props.recommendations:
• Launch a customer-facing portal within 90 days where customers can view their licenses, check usage, and manage renewals — 61% of customers want this, and it reduces support tickets by 30–40%
  • Introduce at least one flexible pricing model that lets customers scale up or down — 69% of customers demand this flexibility, and rigid terms are a top reason for churn
  • Create a customer feedback loop specifically about licensing — quarterly surveys or win/loss analysis on pricing objections will reveal quick wins you're currently missing

props.insight: Reasonable flexibility. Let customers adjust their plans post-purchase to improve retention.
props.whatItMeans: {company} is meeting basic customer expectations but has room to improve. Self-service capabilities and real-time usage visibility are becoming table stakes. 42% of vendors are already implementing self-service portals.
props.recommendations:
• Let customers choose their deployment model at the time of use, not just at purchase — 35% of vendors now support this, and it eliminates a common deal blocker
  • Build customer-facing usage dashboards that show value delivered — customers who can see how much they're using your software are 2–3x more likely to renew and expand

props.insight: Strong alignment. Deploy predictive analytics to identify upsell and churn signals proactively.
props.whatItMeans: {company} demonstrates strong customer alignment in licensing. Your customers likely appreciate the flexibility and visibility you provide. Focus on predictive capabilities to maintain this advantage.
props.recommendations:
• Innovate on customer-centric packaging — let customers build custom bundles or mix-and-match features rather than choosing from fixed tiers
  • Deploy predictive analytics on usage data to identify at-risk renewals 60–90 days in advance, and trigger proactive engagement before churn conversations begin

props.action: Launch a self-service license management portal
props.detail: 61% of customers want better visibility into their licenses. A self-service portal reduces support burden, increases transparency, and directly addresses the #1 customer complaint.
Your customer alignment is strong. Use usage data to predict churn 60–90 days in advance and trigger proactive engagement to protect and expand existing revenue.

props.insight: Selling products independently leaves revenue on the table. Start with a simple 2-product bundle.
props.whatItMeans: {company} is likely leaving significant revenue on the table by selling each product independently. Without a portfolio strategy, you miss cross-sell opportunities, and your sales team lacks the tools to drive larger deals.
props.recommendations:
• Create your first product bundle this quarter — pick your two most complementary products, offer a 10–15% discount when purchased together, and track the impact on deal size
  • Draft a one-page portfolio monetization strategy document — define which products can be bundled, which have cross-sell potential, and what a target enterprise agreement looks like
  • Calculate how much revenue you're leaving on the table from customers who buy only one product but could benefit from others — this number builds the internal business case for investment

props.insight: Good progress. Formalize with centralized pricing governance across product lines.
props.whatItMeans: {company} has started exploring portfolio monetization. The opportunity now is to formalize this — build centralized pricing governance and create standardized bundle frameworks.
props.recommendations:
• Establish a central pricing committee that governs cross-product pricing — 69% of successful portfolio strategies include this, and it prevents internal teams from undercutting each other
  • Build an integrated licensing framework that allows multi-product deals with shared terms, credits, or volume discounts — make it easy for sales to construct large deals

props.insight: Well-developed strategy. Evolve toward enterprise-wide agreements with shared credit pools.
props.whatItMeans: {company}'s portfolio monetization approach is well-developed. Consider evolving toward enterprise-wide agreements and shared credit pools to deepen customer commitment.
props.recommendations:
• Design enterprise-wide agreements with shared credit pools that incentivize customers to expand across your portfolio — this increases switching costs and deepens relationships
  • Implement portfolio-level analytics to identify which product combinations drive the highest lifetime value, then optimize your bundle strategy around those patterns

props.action: Create your first cross-product bundle or enterprise agreement
props.detail: 74% of vendors say cross-portfolio agreements would be very useful. Start with your two most complementary products — even a simple bundle can increase average deal size by 20–30%.
Your portfolio monetization is on track. Formalize with centralized pricing governance to prevent internal conflicts and enable faster go-to-market for new bundles.

props.insight: Manual processes create cost overhead and slow customer onboarding. Automate provisioning first.
props.whatItMeans: Manual licensing processes at {company} are creating costs, delays, and errors that directly impact customer experience. Only 10% of vendors are fully automated, but those that are report faster order fulfillment and lower operational overhead.
props.recommendations:
• Automate license key generation and provisioning first — this single change can cut order-to-activation time from days to minutes and eliminate the most common source of customer frustration
  • Consolidate your licensing data into one system within 6 months — only 25% of vendors have achieved this, but without it you can't accurately forecast, identify churn risk, or make data-driven decisions
  • Replace manual renewal tracking with automated workflows — every missed renewal is lost revenue, and manual processes mean renewals slip through the cracks at scale

props.insight: Partially automated. Consolidate licensing data into one platform for better forecasting.
props.whatItMeans: {company} has made progress on automation but still has significant manual touchpoints. 63% of vendors cite too many disparate systems as a top barrier — consolidation should be a priority.
props.recommendations:
• Move off custom in-house licensing tools to a dedicated platform — 61% of vendors still rely on proprietary tools that become a bottleneck as product complexity grows
  • Automate entitlement tracking and reconciliation across business units so you have a real-time view of what every customer is entitled to use vs. what they're actually using

props.insight: Strong automation. Use your data for predictive churn detection and automated upsell triggers.
props.whatItMeans: {company}'s operations are well-automated, giving you a cost advantage and better customer experience than most peers. Use your operational data proactively with predictive churn models.
props.recommendations:
• Build predictive models on your licensing data to automatically flag upsell opportunities, at-risk renewals, and usage anomalies — turn your operational data into a revenue engine
  • Implement real-time usage collection across all deployment models (including on-premises) so you can offer true consumption-based pricing to any customer, anywhere

props.action: Automate license provisioning and renewal workflows
props.detail: Only 10% of vendors are fully automated. Automating provisioning alone can cut order-to-activation time from days to minutes, directly improving customer experience and reducing ops costs.

props.action: Build predictive analytics on licensing data
props.detail: Your operations are strong. Turn your data into a revenue engine with predictive models that flag upsell opportunities, at-risk renewals, and usage anomalies automatically.

props.insight: Without an AI pricing strategy, you risk giving away value. Define tiered AI pricing now.
props.whatItMeans: {company} has not yet developed a strategy for monetizing AI features. With 76% of vendors rethinking licensing specifically because of AI, this gap will widen quickly. Software buyers expect AI to be priced transparently.
props.recommendations:
• Define an AI pricing strategy within 30 days — even if your AI features aren't ready yet, having a pricing framework prevents the default of giving AI value away for free when you do launch
  • Study how your top 3 competitors are pricing AI features — 60% of vendors have already added AI capabilities, and customers will compare your approach to theirs
  • Start with simple AI tiering: offer a basic AI experience in your standard plan and reserve advanced AI features for a premium tier — this captures value without complex metering

props.insight: Basic AI monetization in place. Build usage metering to enable consumption-based pricing.
props.whatItMeans: {company} has begun addressing AI monetization but has room to formalize the approach. The vendors who pull ahead here will tie AI pricing to measurable outcomes or consumption metrics.
props.recommendations:
• Move beyond simple bundling — implement AI-specific add-on pricing or tiered access that lets power users pay more while casual users get basic AI included
  • Build usage metering for AI features now (API calls, compute tokens, predictions served) so you have the infrastructure ready for consumption-based pricing as AI adoption grows

props.insight: Leading-edge approach. Pioneer outcome-based AI pricing tied to business results delivered.
props.whatItMeans: {company} is among the leading vendors in AI monetization readiness. Your ability to price AI features based on usage or outcomes positions you to capture significantly more value from AI investments.
props.recommendations:
• Pioneer outcome-based AI pricing for your most impactful AI features — charge based on business results delivered (deals closed, defects prevented, hours saved) rather than compute consumed
  • Implement dynamic AI pricing that adjusts based on model complexity and resource consumption — as newer, more expensive AI models are released, your pricing should scale proportionally

props.action: Define your AI feature monetization strategy
props.detail: 76% of vendors say AI is driving new licensing considerations. If you're adding AI features without a pricing strategy, you're giving away value. Even basic tiering (free/premium) captures more revenue than bundling AI for free.

props.action: Implement usage-based metering for AI features
props.detail: Your AI monetization is ahead of most peers. Implement consumption metering (API calls, tokens, compute) to capture upside from power users and align price with value.

props.upliftText: Organizations at your maturity level have the most headroom for growth. By addressing the fundamentals — flexible pricing, automation, and portfolio bundling — you could unlock significant revenue that is currently being left on the table through rigid licensing and manual processes.

You have solid growth potential. 55% of vendors in a similar position expect 6–10% revenue uplift from implementing a full portfolio monetization strategy, with 19% expecting more than 10%. Prioritizing automation and cross-portfolio licensing will deliver the fastest returns.

Your organization is positioned to capture meaningful incremental revenue by optimizing your existing approach. The biggest opportunities lie in advanced pricing models (usage-based, outcome-based) and deeper cross-portfolio integration.

As a mature organization, your gains will come from optimization rather than transformation. Focus on AI monetization, predictive analytics for upsell, and innovative pricing models to capture premium value.
